full_judgment:
2. Defendants contested the suit by filing a joint written statement. Their claim is that Habib Bank Limited advanced Taka 20,00,000 in 1968 against under writing shares of Rajshahi Sugar Mills Ltd, that the company issued shares in favour of the Habib Bank Ltd, that the suit was filed on untrue allegations of fact which is liable to be dismissed and that the amount of liability was adjusted long ago with Habib Bank Ltd. Karachi Branch Plaintiffs has examined Ruhul Amin Chowdhury (PW 1) and Abul Hasnat (PW 2) in support of its case. The defendants have examined one witness Md Nasir (DW 1), the Managing Director of Habib Oil Mills Ltd. The learned Subordinate Judge on consideration of evidence on record by judgment and order dated 20th November 1990 dismissed the suit holding that the suit is barred by limitation. 

 4. Mr Abdur Razzaque Khan, the learned Advocate appearing for the defendants-respondents, on the other hand, submits that the suit as framed is not maintainable, inasmuch as, the transaction was entered in 1968 when there was no provision for equitable mortgage by deposit of title deeds in the district of Dhaka and therefore, the suit for selling the mortgaged property is not legally maintainable. Mr Khan further argues even if it is assumed that the defendant No. 1 has availed the cash credit no facility of Taka 20,00,000, the suit for recovery of the outstanding liability is hopelessly barred by limitation as the plaintiff has not instituted the suit within the statutory period of limitation. 

 11. The plaintiff stated in paragraph 10 of the plaint that it requested the defendant No. 1 to make payment of outstanding liability by letter dated 1st October 1977 but the defendant No. 1 refused to pay by letter dated 15th October, 1977 (Exhibit Ja). There is no other statement in the plaint that after the expiry of the date of payment, there was any correspondence between them regarding the payment. The plaintiff did not make any demand for payment prior to 1st October, 1977 to the defendants. If the defendants fail to make payment within the stipulated time, the plaintiff is required to file the suit for recovery of the outstanding loan with interest within a period of three years from the date of expiry of the last date of payment of installments as per Exhibit 'Cha'. The last date for payment expired on 30th June 1973 and the period of limitation reckoned from that date which expired on 30th June 1976. Therefore, the plaintiffs claim for recovery of money is hopelessly barred by limitation. The learned Subordinate Judge, in the premises, is perfectly justified in dismissing the suit by holding that the suit is barred by limitation. We find no merit in this appeal.
